name: markov_chains
doc: A MISSING STICK, 2026-11-25 (the stick audit): the Monte Carlo stick names stick_markov_chains_and_mcmc, which was never minted. Three seals on one small chain the engine re-derives through its mathematics verifier's numeric check (its stationary distribution, detailed balance, its mixing), an instance mark on each, and a note on what MCMC is and where it ties.

sticks.question: Markov chains and MCMC
sticks.statement: A Markov chain moves between states with probabilities that depend only on the present state; a finite chain that is irreducible and aperiodic settles to one stationary distribution whatever state it starts in. Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samples a target distribution by building a chain whose stationary distribution is that target.
references: N. Metropolis, A. W. Rosenbluth, M. N. Rosenbluth, A. H. Teller, E. Teller, J. Chem. Phys. 21 (1953) 1087-1092
sticks.by: Narrow Highway - a missing stick, Markov chains, 2026-11-25

marks.claim: [the stationary distribution, SEALED] A two-state chain that leaves state 1 with probability a = 0.1 and state 2 with probability b = 0.5 spends, in the long run, the share b/(a + b) = 0.5/0.6 = 0.8333 of its time in state 1 (sealed), whatever state it starts in. The chain forgets where it began; that forgetting is what makes it a sampler.

[detailed balance, SEALED] At that distribution the flow from state 1 to state 2, pi_1 a = (5/6)(0.1), equals the flow back, pi_2 b = (1/6)(0.5): their ratio is 1 (sealed). Metropolis (1953) and Hastings (1970) build a chain to satisfy exactly this balance for a chosen target, so that the target is its stationary distribution.

[how fast it forgets, SEALED] The chain's second eigenvalue is 1 - a - b = 0.4, so its distance from the stationary distribution shrinks by that factor at every step: after 10 steps it is 0.4^10 = 1.05e-4 of where it began (sealed). A chain whose second eigenvalue is near 1 mixes slowly - the practical limit of every MCMC run.

[where it ties] The Monte Carlo stick names this one, and the Yang-Mills stick already holds two witnesses on this same chain (its fixed point and its balance, from the Markov-chain reading). MCMC is a Monte Carlo method that draws its samples by walking a Markov chain instead of drawing them independently. Lattice gauge theory computes its numbers this way (stick_yang_mills_existence_and_mass_gap). That a finite, irreducible, aperiodic chain converges to its one stationary distribution is a theorem (Perron-Frobenius); the samples are evidence about the target, and the seals here are the arithmetic of one small chain, never the convergence of a large one.
